- F-238 **Under walk, two generic declarations a pair of whose parameter types excluded only in walk's reading of each at one symbolic instantiation are read each over its own instances, and are valid only by the No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet Rules on their declared domains.** Walk's load check read two generic functions of one name and one list of static parameters at one shared symbolic instantiation (`FGenericFunction.java:43-64`), and two instances of one generic object as two types that cannot be extended. Now such an exclusion is withdrawn where the instances of each do not exclude (instances of one generic type exclude only where their static arguments cannot be equal; an exclusion read at the shared instantiation stands where every generic type both extend forces one instance, as `Array` and `ImmutableArray` through `ReadableArray`), and the pair is then refused where each domain is inside the other, valid where one is inside the other with its return type below at the holding instance where that instance stands for every instance applicable to an argument of the inner one (F-252), or where a third declaration inside both holds their overlap (F-bounds read from the declarations, a symbolic size unified with a size parameter as `types/SymbolicNat.unifyStaticArg` reads it); otherwise refused, "with generic type, at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types" (F-155). A pair that excludes only through a static argument that another position fixes is refused (row 740). Gated by `tests/GenericBoundsNoMeetWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleSizeWalk`, `GenericOverloadInstancesApartWalk` (refused), `GenericBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericFBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericPairExcludingWalk`, `GenericSizePairNestedWalk` and `ShuffleTest` (load), and `XXXGenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-overload-if/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 9.
- F-252 **Under walk, two functions with static parameters that no pair of parameter types excludes are read on their declared domains, each over its own instances, by the No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet Rules, and a pair whose declared domains are equal is refused even where the parameter check orders it.** Walk's parameter-by-parameter check passes a pair it finds excluding; a pair of two own generics it refuses is read by `genericPairValid` (`interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:766`), whether or not an exclusion was withdrawn; a pair it passes by order, one at least an own generic and the other an own generic or plain, whose declared domains each lie inside the other is refused, "fails because their parameter lists have the same types" (`:533-540`, `sameDeclaredDomains` `:806`), since the check reads a type parameter as strictly below its bound. Limits: the Meet Rule's search matches the two domains only where their parameter types are, position by position, instances of one generic type or static parameters (row 539); a pair whose parameter types exclude only together is refused (row 740); instances of one generic type at different ground arguments do not exclude in the check (row 416); a generic functional method is compared on the instance a call makes, and so is a generic dotted method except where exactly one of the two declared domains lies inside the other (F-253). Gated by `tests/DispatchRenamedGenericArmWalk`, `DispatchSwappedGenericArmWalk`, `GenericPairNestedBoundsWalk` (load and dispatch), `GenericBesideGenericSameDomain`, `GenericBesidePlainSameDomain` (refused), `XXXOverloadExistentialMeetWalk` and `XXXGenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-generic-pairs/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5. The Return Type Rule, where one of two own generics lies inside the other, is read at the instance of the outer one that holds the inner one's declared domain only where that instance stands for every instance applicable to an argument of the inner one (`returnRuleAtEveryInstance`, `OverloadedFunction.java` at 36afa7eb1): each static parameter the outer one's return type names is fixed by a static argument of one of its parameter types, or the outer one returns that type parameter and the inner one returns a type parameter of its own that is the type of no other parameters, or has there an object type below which its return type lies; otherwise the pair is refused, "at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types", as `f[\T extends Shape\](x: T, y: T): T` beside `f[\U extends Round\](x: U, y: Round): Round` and `f[\T extends Shape\](x: T): Box[\T\]` beside `f[\U extends Round\](x: U): Box[\U\]` are, which the compiled checker refuses too. Gated by `tests/GenericReturnRuleOuterParamWalk`, `GenericReturnRuleInvariantWalk` (refused) and `GenericReturnRuleHoldsWalk` (load and dispatch). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-generic-pairs/SKEPTIC.md` section 2. A type parameter bounded by `Any` counts: `g[\T\](a: T)` beside `g(a: Any)` is refused as equal declared domains, which the compiled checker accepts (row 759).
- F-253 **Under walk, a dotted call that writes no static argument infers a generic method's own static arguments, and the method is chosen on its declared domain.** Walk takes the instance from the arguments' run-time types, as at a call of a generic function, whether the method is alone under its name or among its receiver's overloads. Against another method of the set it is compared on its declared domain where exactly one of the two declared domains lies inside the other, as an own generic is. A method that a trait declares is the exception: its bounds are not read where they are declared, so a type parameter that is a parameter's whole type takes the join of the arguments' run-time types with no argument converted, and a bounded one that nothing fixes takes `BottomType` (row 766, `XXXTraitGenericMethodInference`). Rung L's generic `distribute` then runs the nested reductions under walk (F-248). Gated by `tests/MethodStaticArgInference.fss`, `MethodStaticArgOverloadedReceiver.fss`, `MethodStaticArgDeclaredDomain.fss` and `NestedReductionFusion.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-method-sargs/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 2.

A generic instance chosen by converting an argument dispatches again, except for overloaded methods. The symbolic instance reads the static parameters' kinds and bounds, not a `where` clause. So hash maps and sets of nodes that hold neither kind below iterate in one order whatever code asked for an identity hash before, and so do the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` takes in turn. Two kinds of node still hash by identity, and so does every node that holds one: the inference variables, whose id is a bare `Object` (`nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1166-1184`), through which no output of the count stage moves, and walk's `_WrappedFValue` (`interpreter/evaluator/_WrappedFValue.java:170-177`; row 430). `DeclaredFunction`s still hash by identity, but since row 737's repair no choice of `ApiTypeExtractor` depends on their order (F-254). # The C series and the APL side quest: state and what comes next

## Where the work stands

Retired on 2026-10-12: the current state of the work is the first section of `coordinator/PLAN.md`, and what is in flight is `coordinator/BOOT.md`; the text this section held is in `microgpt-run-c-handover-history.md`, "The first section as retired on 2026-10-12".

## Read first

`explorations/coordinator/README.md`, `FACTS.md` and `POSITIONS.md` first (created 2026-09-15): the established facts and Pavol's positions, so that nothing there is re-derived or re-explained. Then the rest of this section.

*Superseded in part, 2026-09-26:* the work branch is `main`, pushed and then fast-forwarded to `claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` (protocol § 4); the sealed-tree rule ended with the unsealing of 2026-09-17 (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`); stop-hook reminders are declined silently (protocol § 4). The rest of this paragraph is from the C series' era. `explorations/protocol.md` is the operating manual and stays in force: Opus workers for probes, exploration, replication, runs and compilation; design, implementation and articles in this thread; worker code reviewed against the design before it is committed; Pavol decides. Work branch `claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr`; commit and push as you go; fast-forward `main` after every push with `git push origin claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr:main`; if `main` diverged because Pavol committed there, merge `origin/main` into the work branch, never rewrite history. The only other branches this thread pushes to are `claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` (the Fable session's branch, when Pavol asks) and, when asked, `transcripts`, `blinded-fable`, `transcripts-blinded`. Commit footer exactly the two lines in protocol.md; no model identifier in any committed file except the process records' "models" row. Never modify the historical language, compiler, runtime or shipped library ("we are not unsealing anything"). Never commit copyrighted decks or Karpathy's `microgpt.py`. Plain register: short sentences, no flourish, no caveats that are not real problems, no headers under 500 words. AskUserQuestion is broken here; artifact watch subscriptions are refused. A worker cancelled by Pavol is not resumed or relaunched unless he asks. Commit in-progress snapshots when the stop hook nags, with "worker running" in the message. Pavol's standing objection, answered once: the programs contain no explicit threading; every `for` is Fortress's implicitly parallel loop on the runtime's work-stealing pool

content.content:
static parameters whose arguments have several minimal common supertypes in
favour of any other declaration applicable to the call without coercion
(row~589 of the revival's gap ledger).
It fixes a type parameter by the expected type only at a reduction or a
comprehension that writes no static argument and whose value is that of a
local variable declared with a type or of a top-level or local function
declared with a return type, as the box after the list in
\secref{numeral-default} says; elsewhere it does not yet fix a type parameter
by the expected type.
A type parameter that an argument bounds only from above, as a function
argument bounds the type parameter of its parameter type, it instantiates at the
intersection of the upper bounds that its declared bound and the arguments
place on it: at \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} for a function of a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} where
the type parameter is declared without an \KWD{extends} clause, and at
\TYP{Number} for a function of an \TYP{Any} where it is bounded by
\TYP{Number}; such a type parameter whose bound mentions a
static parameter, or that is declared with several bounds that it cannot meet,
it still instantiates at \TYP{BottomType}; and where the arguments place on
such a type parameter two upper bounds that it cannot meet, as a function over
one trait and a function over another do when neither trait extends the other,
the call fails with an error of unification (row~616 of the revival's gap ledger).
It infers the static arguments of a generic dotted method that a call does not
write as it infers a generic function's, whether the method is alone under its
name or among the overloads of its receiver, and compares declarations with
static parameters on the parameter types they declare, generic dotted methods
among them; but it stops at load on an object or trait that declares a generic
dotted method beside a plain one of the same name (row~760 of the revival's
gap ledger), and it stops on an object that extends a generic trait whose
dotted method has a static parameter of its own bounded by the trait's, at load
or at a generic object's first instance (row~762).
A generic dotted method that a trait declares it instantiates without reading
the bounds where they are declared: a type parameter that is the whole type of
parameters takes the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments'
run-time types, and no argument is converted, so that a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and
a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} give \TYP{AnyIntegral}, and a bounded type parameter that
nothing fixes takes \TYP{BottomType} (row~766).
It dispatches a converted call again, except a call of an overloaded method.}

\section{A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie}

content.content:
### 3.1 Row 765: an inherited generic functional method beside an object's own plain one

`SkFunctional` fails on a `Square` under walk, old and new alike, with both declarations' dotted forms in the `OverloadedMethod` the message prints; the compiled path stops at compile with row 724's `ClassCastException`. Row 723 is the pair declared in the object, which stops at load; this pair loads and fails at the call. It is the functional-method sibling of `MethodStaticArgDeclaredDomain`, outside row 21 and the rung's claim, so I recorded it (home 2: the specification makes the generic applicable to a `Square`, `basic/overloading.tex`, "Applicability to Named Functional Calls").

### 3.2 Row 766: a trait's generic dotted method, instantiated without coercion or bound

`SkCoerce`, `SkTraitU` and `SkTraitBound` show that a generic dotted method that a trait declares is not instantiated as a generic function or an object's own method is. A `ZZ32` and a `ZZ64` give `Box[\AnyIntegral\]` with the `ZZ32` kept, where the specification takes "the narrowest type into which every one of them converts: ZZ64 for a ZZ32 and a ZZ64" and coerces the `ZZ32` (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:84-86`), as the compiled path does (`over z w: [3:ZZ64,4:ZZ64]`) and as walk's own box says it does. A bounded type parameter that nothing fixes gives `Box[\BOTTOM\]`, where "Inference never instantiates a static parameter at BottomType" (`:104`). `SkFailG`'s 'abm=K=(Int,Any)' shows the bound was not met into the inference where it is declared. The inference reads bounds and coercion targets in `appliedThing.getWithin()` (`EvaluatorBase.java:557`, `:633-634`), which for a trait's generic method is the trait's member environment (`BuildTraitEnvironment.java:42-44`), the environment the probe's section 2 calls empty; part A passes the evaluation environment as `envForInference`, which those lines do not read. I did not trace it further. The repair is in `EvaluatorBase.java`, which the brief gives no rung of this batch, or in how a trait's `GenericMethod` is made, the team's code, so it is a deferred defect (home 2), not a fix of this change. The written form converts (`SkTraitWritten`), and an object's own method converts beside an inherited overload (`SkCoerce5`).

XXXTraitGenericMethodInference.fss:35:20-34:`, ` OK Saw expected exception`;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`). Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the
record file and its history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
